source.title: Freshwater Shrimp Diversity and its Correlation to Water Properties in Selected Sites of Cañas River in Cavite, Philippines
source.provider: CvSU Research Journal; Cavite State University

access.method: Official CvSU journal archive identifies the article in its July–December 2022 issue; official PDF text was opened and reviewed through indexed document extraction.
access.limitations: The local shell could not resolve ovpre.cvsu.edu.ph, so no local PDF receipt or hash was produced. Coordinates are mentioned as included with the selected-site figure but were not visually reviewed or transcribed.

bibliographicFishStudyLead.title: Identification of fish and crustacean species and water quality assessment of Cañas River watershed, Cavite, Philippines
bibliographicFishStudyLead.decision: This is a bibliographic retrieval lead that strengthens the existing 2017 fish-study lead. The citation contains no fish names, field data or reuse terms and does not establish that conference listings are the same work.

studyDesign.reportedScope: Four selected Cañas River watershed sites; three 10 m by 10 m transects per site, separated by 10 m and parallel to water flow.
studyDesign.captureMethod: Dip-frame nets and shrimp traps placed at the benthic substrate; bait described as fish heads/meat and toasted coconut meat.
studyDesign.identificationMethod: Morphological identification using Carpenter and Niem (1998) and Motoh (1980); the article says identifications were verified by an invertebrate curator at the University of the Philippines Diliman Institute of Biology museum.
studyDesign.waterbodyCrosswalk: The paper places the named sites within the Cañas River study scope. No main-channel/tributary geometry or exact station-point crosswalk was established here; the named-site locality strings are retained without coordinates.
studyDesign.sourceTerminologyCaveat: The paper calls the taxa freshwater shrimps. No salinity measurements or ecological-origin evaluation were used in this review, so no species is classified as freshwater-only, native, introduced, or marine/brackish.

qualityReview.sourceInternalCountConflict: The abstract, results, conclusion and Table 1 support six taxa, but one introductory sentence says seven crustacean species. Retain six only as the internally repeated table/result count and keep the source discrepancy visible.

taxonomyCrosscheck.scope: Nomenclatural matching only; GBIF matches do not independently verify the article's field identifications or specimens.

rights.policyFinding: CvSU's journal publishing workflow says an accepted manuscript is accompanied by a Copyright Form; no article-specific license or permission for redistribution of the extracted species table was located.
rights.decision: Keep minimally attributed source findings in the research ledger. Do not reproduce the article table, figures or prose, and do not publish species rows in Bangwit until item-specific reuse rights and product taxonomic scope are confirmed.

limitations: The paper is an undated, selected-site shrimp survey, not a fish checklist or a complete inventory of the Cañas watershed.
Taxon counts are reported at four named site aggregates; they are not point observations or abundance estimates for the entire river.
The source's introduction has a six-versus-seven crustacean discrepancy; source table and results list six.
One source name is a GBIF Backbone synonym; preserve Litopenaeus vannamei as the original spelling and show the accepted-name crosswalk only as taxonomy metadata.
No water salinity, native status, present-day presence, legal catchability, access, safety, channel boundary or coordinate was established by this review.
Item-specific reuse terms and permission to publish a derived species list remain unresolved.
nextAction: Seek authorized access to the 2017 CvSU fish-and-crustacean thesis cited by this article, request item-specific reuse terms for the journal article, and visually inspect its sampling-site map only if exact coordinate/location work is needed. Keep the six shrimp rows research-only and continue the separate fish-evidence and channel-geometry gap.
